To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
elevated levels of plasma BDNF and platelet derived growth factor AA are associated with high CBF velocity (TCD velocity) and stroke in children and adults with sickle cell disease.

plasma BDNF and plasma PDGF-AA levels were higher in subjects with high TCD velocities and in SCA subjects who had strokes than in subjects with normal TCD velocities and non- SCA subjects who did not have strokes.

plasma brain-derived neurotropic factor and platelet-derived growth factor-AA levels are associated both with abnormal cerebral blood flow velocity in the middle cerebral artery and with stroke in children with SCA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of BDNF and other growth factors in the cerebrovascular disease that is common in children with sick cell anemia.
the development of biomarkers to aid in the prediction and prevention of stroke in SCA.
the pathophysiology of stroke in children with Sickle Cell Disease (SCD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
elevated BDNF levels in children with SCA are associated with high CBF velocity (abnormal TCD), and elevated PDGF-AA levels predict risk for stroke.
BDNF and especially PDGF-AA are associated with high CBF velocity in children with SCA.
elevated BDNF, and PDGF-AA are good predictors of high TCD velocity in children with SCA and that elevated PDGF-AA is also a good predictor of stroke development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BDNF and/or PDGF-AA are good predictors of the development of high TCD velocity in SCA patients.
BDNF and/or PDGF-AA may be useful as markers to predict stroke in sickle cell anemias.
BDNF and platelet derived growth factor-AA are associated with high CBF velocity in SCA and that PDGF-AA may be associated with risk for stroke.
The main takeaway from our work is that
plasma BDNF and plasma PDGF-AA are biomarkers of cerebrovascular complications in SCA and can be used to predict stroke and high TCD in SCA patients.
BDNF, a growth factor known to promote neuronal survival and neurogenesis, is associated with stroke in children with SCA.

elevated BDNF, which is a neuro-protective factor, and PDGF-AA, a growth factor that is involved in the pathogenesis of cerebrovascular remodeling, may contribute to the pathophysiology of cerebrovascular complications in SCA.
